newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to ask new British PM for Parthenon marbles.
newsitem.headline: Greece to ask new British PM for Parthenon marbles.

text.p: Greece will ask Britain's newly-elected Labour government to return the Parthenon marbles in a renewed effort to reclaim the classical sculptures from the British Museum in London.
"A letter will be sent to the new British government from the Greek government," the Culture Ministry said in a statement late on Friday.
The return of the 5th century BC artworks, known in England as the Elgin Marbles after the British diplomat who removed them from the Parthenon in 1806, has been a long-standing Greek demand.
The late Greek actress and culture minister Melina Mercouri was believed to have won the sympathy of the Labour Party, then in opposition, with her feisty campaign to bring the marbles home.

Lord Elgin removed the frieze and other parts of the massive Parthenon temple dedicated to the goddess Athena, considered the masterpiece of Greek classical architecture, with permission from the local Ottoman Turkish administrators.
Those who oppose the return of the marbles say the British Museum has safeguarded them from pollution while other sculptures on the Acropolis have been damaged by Athens' notorious smog.
Greece has said it will build a new museum at the foot of the Acropolis hill to house them. The Italian-designed museum is scheduled to finish in about three years.

The ministry said that apart from the letter to new Prime Minister Tony Blair, Culture Minister Evangelos Venizelos would also raise the issue with his British counterpart during a European Union meeting in Luxembourg on June 30.
